title: Find two values that add up to a target
summary: Guests arrive one at a time; find two whose ticket numbers add up to a target by remembering everyone already seen.
goal: Find two guests whose numbers add up to the target

examples.label: Two equal numbers
examples.explanation: Two different guests can wear the same number: 3 + 3 = 6.

examples.label: No pair
examples.explanation: No two guests add up to 10, so there is no answer.

ladder.name: Check every pair
ladder.idea: For each guest, compare their number with every guest who arrived after them.

ladder.name: Sort, then squeeze from both ends
ladder.idea: Sort the guests by number while remembering their positions, then use two pointers from the ends.
ladder.insight: If the numbers were in order, two pointers could rule out one guest per step, as in the gift-voucher lesson.

ladder.name: Ticket book (hash map)
ladder.idea: For each guest, the partner they need is `target − number`. Look that up in a book of everyone already seen, then write this guest down.
ladder.insight: The partner a guest needs is fully determined by their number. A lookup table answers "has that number arrived?" in one step, with no sorting.

approaches.name: Ticket book (hash map)
approaches.summary: Look up the needed partner, then write the guest down.

transfer.problem: A shop lists item prices in no particular order. Find two different items that together cost exactly a gift card's value.
transfer.explanation: The order is arbitrary and you need a pair with an exact total: for each item, look up whether its complement has been seen.

selfCheck: Looks up the partner before writing the current value down, so a value never pairs with itself.
Returns no answer when no pair exists.
Uses one pass and a map, not two nested loops.
